p01.why: alignas must not apply to a parameter.

p02.why: alignas on an alias declaration; GCC 14 accepts, GCC 16, Clang, and EDG reject (Q-0072).

p03.why: The definition has a different alignment from the earlier declaration, which Clang and EDG reject and GCC accepts (Q-0070).

p04.why: The operand has floating-point type, which every compiler rejects.

p05.why: alignas(0) has no effect, so S keeps the alignment of int.

p06.why: Objects in static and automatic storage get the 4096 alignment of their type, so main returns 0.

p07.why: 3 is not a power of two.

p08.why: Outer takes the 64 alignment of its member Inner, Inner starts at offset 64, and the size rounds to 128.

p10.why: The class alignment is 32 and its size is a multiple of its alignment, so 32.

p11.why: The definition leaves out the alignas of the earlier declaration; reading ALN-3 as a mismatch, Clang and EDG reject and GCC accepts (Q-0070), but the specification does not say this case directly.

p12.why: Both declarations have the same alignment, 16.

p13.why: An enumerator of a scoped enumeration; Clang and GCC reject, EDG converts it and accepts (Q-0313).

p14.why: An unscoped enumerator is a valid operand, and its value 8 is a power of two.

p15.why: A class operand with a constexpr conversion to int; Clang and EDG accept, GCC rejects (Q-0314).

p16.why: A definition can add alignas when the earlier declaration has none.

p17.why: alignas must not apply to a function.

p18.why: Different alignments across units need no diagnostic, every compiler accepts, and get returns 0, so main returns 0.

p19.why: The strictest of several alignas is 16, but GCC uses the last one on a class, 8, so GCC fails the static_assert (Q-0071).

p20.why: The operand must be a constant expression, and n is not.

p21.why: alignas on a variable does not change its type, so decltype(x) is int.

p22.why: -8 is not zero or a positive power of two.

p23.why: The declaration and the definition give different alignments; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0070).

p24.why: Each S has size 16, so an array of three has size 48.

p25.why: The largest extended alignment is implementation-defined; EDG 7.0 rejects 2^28, Clang and GCC accept.

p26.why: The definition leaves out the alignas of the earlier declaration; read as a mismatch, Clang and EDG reject and GCC accepts (Q-0070).

p27.why: alignas(1) is weaker than the alignment of int; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts and keeps the natural alignment (Q-0069).

p28.why: new gives objects and arrays with extended alignment the alignment of their type, so main returns 0.

p29.why: alignas(1) is weaker than the alignment of double; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0069).

p30.why: v starts at offset 8, the class alignment is 8, and its size is 16.

p31.why: The static buffer and the automatic local get their declared alignments, so main returns 0.

p32.why: On the x86-64 Linux targets long double has alignment 16, and long long has 8.

p33.why: alignas on a typedef; GCC 14 accepts, GCC 16, Clang, and EDG reject (Q-0072).

p34.why: alignas on an enumeration; EDG 7.0 and GCC 14 accept, Clang and GCC 16 reject (Q-0073).

p35.why: alignas on a bit-field; GCC 14 accepts, GCC 16, Clang, and EDG reject (Q-0072).
